quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Customer Satisfaction Score Measured Selectively] The airline reports a customer satisfaction score based on surveys sent only to passengers whose flights arrived on time, a methodology that excludes the experiences of passengers who faced delays or cancellations, the very situations most likely to generate dissatisfaction, from the overall calculation entirely.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how representative this satisfaction score is of the airline's full customer experience?
options: It likely presents a more favorable picture than surveying all passengers would produce.
Delays and cancellations have no bearing on customer satisfaction.
It would likely be higher if delayed passengers were included.
It accurately reflects the experience of every passenger who flew that year.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely presents a more favorable picture than surveying all passengers would produce.
quests.hint: Think about which passengers are excluded from this survey and what their experiences would likely add to the overall score if included.
quests.explanation: Excluding passengers who experienced delays or cancellations, the situations most likely to lower satisfaction, suggests the reported score presents a more favorable picture than including all passengers would produce.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Study Funded by an Interested Party] The industry-funded study concluding that a particular chemical poses 'no significant health risk at typical exposure levels' uses exposure thresholds that several independent toxicologists argue are set considerably higher than the levels most consumers actually encounter in everyday use, a methodological choice that would tend to understate potential risk.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the study's chosen exposure thresholds?
options: The thresholds have no bearing on the study's conclusions.
They were set lower than typical consumer exposure levels.
They may have been set in a way that makes finding a significant risk less likely.
Independent toxicologists fully endorsed these thresholds.
quests.correctAnswer: They may have been set in a way that makes finding a significant risk less likely.
quests.hint: Think about what setting exposure thresholds higher than real-world levels would do to the likelihood of detecting a risk that actually exists at those real-world levels.
quests.explanation: Toxicologists noting the thresholds exceed typical real-world exposure suggests this methodological choice would make the study less likely to detect risks that exist at the levels consumers actually encounter.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Feature Delayed for 'Quality' Reasons] The software company postpones the release of a promised privacy feature for the third time, each time citing 'ongoing quality assurance,' even as the same release notes announce several unrelated new features shipping on schedule during the same period, a pattern some users interpret as reflecting shifting priorities rather than genuine technical delays.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the company's stated reason for delaying the privacy feature?
options: It clearly explains why every feature has been delayed equally.
It is confirmed as the complete and only reason by the company.
It may not fully explain why this particular feature keeps being delayed while others ship on time.
No other features shipped during the same period.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not fully explain why this particular feature keeps being delayed while others ship on time.
quests.hint: Think about what other features shipping on schedule, while only this one is repeatedly delayed, suggests about the stated 'quality assurance' explanation.
quests.explanation: Other features shipping on schedule while only the privacy feature faces repeated delays suggests the stated 'quality assurance' reason may not fully account for why this specific feature keeps being pushed back.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Species Count That Depends on Definition] Conservationists report that the reserve now hosts '15 percent more species' than a decade ago, a figure that, on closer examination, results partly from a broadened definition of the reserve's boundaries adopted five years ago, which incorporated a neighboring wetland previously counted separately and already known to host a distinct set of species.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how much of this increase reflects genuine new species arriving within the original area?
options: The entire increase reflects genuinely new species arriving in the original area.
A meaningful portion of the reported increase likely reflects the boundary change rather than new arrivals.
The wetland was previously known to host no species at all.
The boundary change had no effect on the reported species count.
quests.correctAnswer: A meaningful portion of the reported increase likely reflects the boundary change rather than new arrivals.
quests.hint: Think about what incorporating an already-populated neighboring area into the count would do to the reported number, separate from any actual ecological change.
quests.explanation: Since the boundary expansion incorporated an already-populated wetland previously counted separately, a meaningful part of the reported increase likely reflects this redefinition rather than new species genuinely arriving in the original reserve.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Craft Described as Dying, Then Revived] A decade-old newspaper article describes a traditional weaving technique as a 'dying art with only a handful of remaining practitioners,' a description now displayed alongside the technique's current thriving cooperative of forty artisans in the region's cultural center, without any update to the original framing that continues to greet visitors.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the accuracy of the displayed description for today's visitors?
options: The cooperative has fewer practitioners now than a decade ago.
The original article was written after the cooperative was formed.
It likely no longer reflects the technique's current, more active status.
It accurately describes the technique's status today.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely no longer reflects the technique's current, more active status.
quests.hint: Compare the decade-old 'dying art' framing with the currently thriving forty-artisan cooperative described alongside it.
quests.explanation: A thriving forty-artisan cooperative existing alongside an unchanged decade-old 'dying art' description suggests the displayed framing has not kept pace with the technique's current, healthier status.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Workplace Wellness Metric That Backfires] After introducing a step-count competition to promote employee wellness, the company's health insurer notes a rise in minor injury claims related to overexertion during the competition period, a pattern that occupational health researchers say sometimes occurs when workplace wellness incentives inadvertently encourage employees to push beyond their usual physical limits.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the step-count competition and the rise in injury claims?
options: Occupational health researchers found this pattern never occurs in wellness programs.
The competition may have unintentionally contributed to employees overexerting themselves.
The competition reduced the number of overexertion injuries.
The competition had no connection to the rise in injuries.
quests.correctAnswer: The competition may have unintentionally contributed to employees overexerting themselves.
quests.hint: Think about what researchers' general observation about wellness incentives, applied to this specific case, suggests about the cause of the rise in claims.
quests.explanation: Researchers noting that wellness incentives can sometimes encourage overexertion, combined with the rise in claims during the competition period, suggests the competition likely contributed to this unintended outcome.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Screening Program's Numbers Reconsidered] Public health officials tout a screening program's success by pointing to a rise in early-stage diagnoses since its launch, a trend some epidemiologists caution may partly reflect the program simply detecting cases that would have eventually been found anyway through routine care, rather than solely representing new cases identified only because of the screening itself.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the epidemiologists' view of the program's reported success?
options: They believe the program has caused new cases of the disease to occur.
They fully endorse attributing the entire rise to the new program.
They believe the reported rise may partly reflect earlier detection of existing cases rather than purely additional cases found.
They believe the program has had no detectable effect on diagnosis rates.
quests.correctAnswer: They believe the reported rise may partly reflect earlier detection of existing cases rather than purely additional cases found.
quests.hint: Think about the distinction epidemiologists draw between detecting cases earlier and detecting cases that otherwise would never have been found.
quests.explanation: Epidemiologists cautioning that the rise may reflect earlier detection of cases eventually found anyway, rather than solely new discoveries, suggests they see the reported success as potentially overstated.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Loan Approval Rate Compared Without Context] The bank publicly reports identical loan approval rates across different neighborhoods in the city, a statistic presented as evidence of equitable lending practices, though consumer advocates note the report does not account for differences in average loan amounts requested or in the specific loan products offered to applicants from each neighborhood.
quests.question: What can be inferred about whether this statistic fully addresses advocates' concerns about equitable lending?
options: Loan amounts and product types are irrelevant to evaluating equity.
It fully resolves any possible concern about equitable lending.
It proves that identical loan products are offered everywhere.
It may not capture other meaningful differences in how lending actually occurs across neighborhoods.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not capture other meaningful differences in how lending actually occurs across neighborhoods.
quests.hint: Think about what factors beyond the approval rate itself, factors the report does not address, might still differ meaningfully between neighborhoods.
quests.explanation: Advocates noting that the report ignores differences in loan amounts and products offered suggests that identical approval rates alone may not fully capture whether lending practices are truly equitable across neighborhoods.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Feature Marketed as Free] The app prominently advertises a key feature as 'completely free to use,' language that remains technically accurate even though accessing the feature requires first subscribing to a separate paid tier that unlocks the app's basic functionality, a detail mentioned only within the settings menu rather than alongside the advertised claim.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the practical accuracy of describing this feature as 'free'?
options: It is entirely accurate with no additional cost of any kind involved.
It is technically true but may create a misleading impression for someone reading the claim alone.
It is completely false in every respect.
The paid tier is prominently mentioned alongside the free claim.
quests.correctAnswer: It is technically true but may create a misleading impression for someone reading the claim alone.
quests.hint: Think about what requiring a separate paid subscription first, a detail tucked away in settings, does to the practical meaning of calling something 'free.'
quests.explanation: While technically true on its own, describing the feature as 'free' without mentioning the required paid subscription, disclosed only deep in settings, suggests the claim could mislead someone about the actual cost involved.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Language Described as Extinct, Prematurely] A widely cited linguistics textbook from twenty years ago lists a regional dialect as 'functionally extinct,' a classification still repeated in more recent academic papers that cite the original textbook directly, even though a documentary team visiting the region five years ago recorded several elderly speakers still using the dialect fluently in daily conversation.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the accuracy of continuing to cite the textbook's original classification?
options: It may perpetuate an outdated conclusion that more recent evidence contradicts.
The documentary team found no speakers of the dialect remaining.
The textbook's classification was updated to reflect the documentary's findings.
It remains fully accurate based on the documentary team's findings.
quests.correctAnswer: It may perpetuate an outdated conclusion that more recent evidence contradicts.
quests.hint: Think about what citing a decades-old classification, without accounting for the documentary team's more recent findings, does to the accuracy of newer academic papers.
quests.explanation: Academic papers continuing to cite the original 'extinct' classification, despite a documentary team finding fluent speakers just five years ago, suggests this repeated citation perpetuates an outdated conclusion rather than reflecting the dialect's actual current status.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Conservation Success Measured in One Dimension] Wildlife officials celebrate a rebounding population of a once-endangered predator as an unqualified conservation success, a framing that overlooks a parallel decline reported by the same agency in two prey species whose populations have fallen sharply since the predator's recovery began, a trade-off the celebratory announcement does not address.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the completeness of describing this situation as an unqualified success?
options: It fully accounts for every ecological change described in the passage.
The agency was unaware of any decline in the prey species.
The prey species populations have also increased alongside the predator's.
It leaves out an ecological trade-off that complicates a simple success narrative.
quests.correctAnswer: It leaves out an ecological trade-off that complicates a simple success narrative.
quests.hint: Think about what the same agency's own reported decline in prey species suggests about calling the predator's recovery an 'unqualified' success.
quests.explanation: The same agency reporting a sharp decline in prey species since the predator's recovery suggests the celebratory framing omits a meaningful ecological trade-off, making 'unqualified success' an incomplete description.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Productivity Study With an Unmentioned Variable] A widely shared study concludes that employees working from a specific open-office layout demonstrate higher measured productivity than those in traditional private offices, a comparison that becomes less clear-cut upon noting the study's open-office group consisted entirely of newly hired employees eager to make a strong impression, while the private-office group included staff with a decade or more of tenure.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the study's conclusion regarding office layout and productivity?
options: Employee tenure has no possible connection to measured productivity.
The study conclusively proves open-office layouts cause higher productivity.
The difference in productivity may be explained by employee tenure rather than the office layout itself.
The two groups were matched equally in terms of tenure and experience.
quests.correctAnswer: The difference in productivity may be explained by employee tenure rather than the office layout itself.
quests.hint: Think about what a systematic difference in tenure between the two groups, separate from the office layout itself, might explain about the productivity gap.
quests.explanation: A newly hired group naturally motivated to impress, compared against a more tenured group, suggests the productivity difference may stem from this tenure gap rather than the office layout the study set out to test.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinical Guideline Updated Slowly] Despite newer research published four years ago suggesting a revised dosage recommendation for a common medication, the professional association's official clinical guideline, still referenced by most prescribing physicians, has not yet been updated, a delay the association attributes to its multi-year formal review process rather than any disagreement with the newer findings.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the guideline currently being followed by most physicians?
options: It may not reflect the most recent research on the appropriate dosage.
The association disputes the validity of the newer research findings.
It has already been fully updated to match the newest research.
It reflects research more recent than what is described in the passage.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not reflect the most recent research on the appropriate dosage.
quests.hint: Think about what a multi-year, still-unfinished review process suggests about whether the current guideline incorporates research from four years ago.
quests.explanation: A guideline still under a multi-year review process, four years after newer dosage research was published, suggests the version most physicians currently reference may not yet reflect the latest findings.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Franchise Fee Disclosed in Stages] The franchise opportunity's initial marketing materials list a starting investment of $150,000, a figure that prospective buyers later learn, only after signing a preliminary agreement and gaining access to the full disclosure document, does not include a required initial inventory purchase, ongoing royalty fees, or a mandatory marketing fund contribution that together can add tens of thousands of dollars to the true first-year cost.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the initial $150,000 figure presented in the marketing materials?
options: It likely understates the true total cost a franchisee should expect to pay initially.
It fully accounts for every cost a franchisee will face in the first year.
It overstates the actual total cost compared to the full disclosure document.
The additional fees are disclosed alongside the initial marketing figure.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely understates the true total cost a franchisee should expect to pay initially.
quests.hint: Think about what several additional required costs, revealed only after signing a preliminary agreement, suggest about the completeness of the original figure.
quests.explanation: Additional required costs disclosed only after a preliminary agreement is signed suggest the initial $150,000 figure understates the true total investment a franchisee should actually expect.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Restaurant Rating System Reconsidered] The city's health inspection scores show a particular restaurant maintaining a consistent 'A' rating for three years, a record its owners frequently cite in advertising, though a closer look at inspection records reveals the restaurant switched to a different, less frequently visited inspection district roughly around the same time its scores began improving.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the improvement in this restaurant's inspection scores?
options: It may be connected to the change in inspection district rather than solely improved practices.
The change in district has no possible bearing on inspection outcomes.
It can only be explained by genuine improvements in food safety practices.
It occurred before the restaurant changed inspection districts.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be connected to the change in inspection district rather than solely improved practices.
quests.hint: Think about what the timing between the district switch and the score improvement suggests about a possible alternative explanation.
quests.explanation: Scores improving around the same time the restaurant switched to a less frequently visited inspection district suggests the improvement may be connected to that change, not only to genuinely improved practices.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An Efficiency Rating Tested Under Ideal Conditions] The appliance's energy efficiency rating, prominently displayed on its packaging, is calculated under standardized laboratory conditions that assume a fixed usage pattern many consumer advocacy groups argue rarely matches how most households actually operate the device, typically resulting in real-world energy consumption noticeably higher than the labeled figure suggests.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the energy consumption most consumers should expect in practice?
options: It is likely higher than the labeled rating implies for a typical household.
It will match the labeled rating precisely for nearly every household.
Usage patterns have no bearing on actual energy consumption.
It will be lower than the labeled rating for most consumers.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely higher than the labeled rating implies for a typical household.
quests.hint: Think about what advocacy groups' observation, that lab conditions rarely match real households, suggests about how the labeled figure compares to actual use.
quests.explanation: Advocacy groups noting that lab conditions rarely reflect typical household usage suggest that real-world energy consumption for most consumers likely exceeds the figure shown on the label.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Recycling Rate That Excludes Contamination] The municipality reports a 65 percent recycling rate, a figure calculated from the total tonnage collected in recycling bins, though waste management officials acknowledge that roughly a third of that collected material is later rejected at sorting facilities due to contamination and ultimately sent to landfill rather than actually recycled.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the actual proportion of collected material that is genuinely recycled?
options: It is likely meaningfully lower than the reported 65 percent collection figure suggests.
It matches the reported 65 percent figure exactly.
It exceeds the reported 65 percent figure once contamination is considered.
Contamination has no effect on how much material is actually recycled.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely meaningfully lower than the reported 65 percent collection figure suggests.
quests.hint: Think about the difference between material collected in recycling bins and material that is actually processed into new products, given the contamination rate mentioned.
quests.explanation: Since roughly a third of collected material is later rejected due to contamination and landfilled instead, the true proportion of material genuinely recycled is likely meaningfully lower than the reported collection-based rate.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Partnership Announced With Selective Emphasis] The joint press release announcing a partnership between the two companies emphasizes shared goals around 'innovation' and 'customer value,' language that offers no specific detail about which company will control key technical decisions, a point that becomes more notable considering the smaller company's technology forms the core of the partnership's product but the larger company retains majority ownership of the resulting venture.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the press release's coverage of control over technical decisions?
options: It fully clarifies which company controls key technical decisions.
It confirms the smaller company retains majority ownership.
It leaves out a detail that could matter significantly to understanding how the partnership will actually function.
Ownership structure has no relevance to how the partnership will operate.
quests.correctAnswer: It leaves out a detail that could matter significantly to understanding how the partnership will actually function.
quests.hint: Think about why omitting details about decision-making control might matter, given the ownership and technology details described.
quests.explanation: Vague language about shared goals, without addressing who controls key technical decisions despite an ownership imbalance, suggests the release omits a detail that could be important to understanding how this partnership will truly operate.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Historical Marker With a Single Perspective] The roadside historical marker describes the battle at this site as a 'decisive victory' without noting whose perspective that description reflects, an omission local historians point out becomes significant once records show the outcome is remembered very differently, as a devastating loss, by descendants of the opposing side who still live in the surrounding region.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the marker's account of the battle?
options: It was written jointly by descendants of both sides of the battle.
It presents one community's perspective as though it were the only or complete account.
It represents a perspective shared equally by all descendants in the region.
Local historians agree completely with the marker's framing.
quests.correctAnswer: It presents one community's perspective as though it were the only or complete account.
quests.hint: Think about what remembering the same event as either a 'victory' or a 'devastating loss,' depending on which descendants you ask, suggests about the marker's single framing.
quests.explanation: Descendants of the opposing side remembering the outcome as a devastating loss suggests the marker's unqualified 'decisive victory' framing reflects only one community's perspective, presented as if it were complete.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Wellness Retreat's Testimonials] The wellness retreat's website features glowing testimonials from past attendees describing transformative results, testimonials the retreat's marketing team selects from a much larger pool of post-stay surveys, a pool that, according to a former employee, also included a substantial number of neutral or critical responses never published anywhere on the site.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the testimonials displayed on the retreat's website?
options: No critical or neutral responses were ever submitted by attendees.
They likely represent a favorable selection rather than the full range of attendee experiences.
They include a balanced mix of critical and positive feedback.
They represent every survey response the retreat has ever received.
quests.correctAnswer: They likely represent a favorable selection rather than the full range of attendee experiences.
quests.hint: Think about what selecting testimonials from a larger pool that included unpublished critical responses suggests about how representative the published ones are.
quests.explanation: A former employee's account of unpublished neutral and critical responses suggests the testimonials shown on the website represent a selectively favorable sample rather than the full range of attendee experiences.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Diversity Report With a Narrow Lens] The company's diversity report highlights significant gains in representation at the entry level over the past three years, a statistic that overshadows a separate figure buried later in the same document showing representation at senior leadership levels has remained essentially unchanged during that same period.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the overall picture the report's emphasis creates?
options: It shows that senior leadership representation improved even more than entry-level figures.
It shows entry-level representation has also remained unchanged.
It may create an impression of broader progress than has actually occurred throughout the organization.
It accurately reflects equal progress at every level of the organization.
quests.correctAnswer: It may create an impression of broader progress than has actually occurred throughout the organization.
quests.hint: Think about what highlighting entry-level gains, while senior-level figures stay flat, does to the overall impression the report creates if a reader only notices the headline statistic.
quests.explanation: Emphasizing entry-level gains while senior leadership figures remain unchanged, a detail placed later in the document, suggests the report's framing may create a more optimistic overall impression than the full data supports.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Cost Comparison That Omits a Category] The manufacturer's comparison chart shows its product priced lower than three named competitors across every listed category, a chart that omits maintenance costs entirely, a category independent reviewers note tends to run significantly higher for this manufacturer's product over a typical five-year ownership period.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the completeness of this cost comparison for a buyer planning long-term ownership?
options: It likely presents an incomplete picture of the true total cost over time.
Independent reviewers found no difference in maintenance costs among these products.
It fully accounts for every relevant cost a long-term owner would face.
Maintenance costs are lower for this product than for the competitors.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely presents an incomplete picture of the true total cost over time.
quests.hint: Think about what leaving out a cost category where this product performs worse, according to independent reviewers, does to the fairness of the overall comparison.
quests.explanation: Omitting maintenance costs, a category where independent reviewers say this product costs more, suggests the manufacturer's chart presents an incomplete picture for buyers considering total ownership cost over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Reforestation Timeline Left Vague] The mining company's environmental restoration plan promises to 'return the land to a natural state following the conclusion of operations,' language that specifies no timeline, no measurable benchmarks, and no independent verification process, details environmental regulators in a neighboring jurisdiction require as standard components of comparable restoration agreements.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the enforceability of this particular restoration promise?
options: Independent verification is already built into this specific promise.
It is just as enforceable as agreements that include specific timelines and benchmarks.
It includes stronger accountability measures than agreements in the neighboring jurisdiction.
It may be difficult to hold the company accountable to, given what it lacks compared to standard agreements elsewhere.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be difficult to hold the company accountable to, given what it lacks compared to standard agreements elsewhere.
quests.hint: Think about what missing a timeline, benchmarks, and independent verification, elements standard elsewhere, suggests about how enforceable this particular promise is.
quests.explanation: Lacking the timeline, benchmarks, and verification process considered standard in a neighboring jurisdiction suggests this restoration promise may be considerably harder to hold the company accountable to.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Feature Comparison That Favors the Reviewer's Sponsor] The technology review site ranks one smartphone model as its top pick for battery life, a ranking that becomes more notable once readers discover, in a disclosure buried at the article's end, that the phone's manufacturer sponsors the site's annual awards event, a relationship not mentioned anywhere near the ranking itself.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the independence of this particular ranking?
options: The manufacturer has no financial relationship with the review site.
It may be worth viewing with some caution given the undisclosed-until-the-end sponsorship relationship.
The sponsorship relationship was prominently disclosed alongside the ranking.
It is entirely independent with no possible conflict of interest.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be worth viewing with some caution given the undisclosed-until-the-end sponsorship relationship.
quests.hint: Think about what a sponsorship relationship, disclosed only at the very end rather than near the ranking, suggests about the ranking's apparent independence.
quests.explanation: A sponsorship relationship disclosed only at the article's end, rather than near the ranking itself, suggests readers encountering just the ranking might reasonably question how independent this particular recommendation truly is.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinical Trial Population That Doesn't Match Patients] The medication's approval was based on a clinical trial population with a median age significantly younger than the population that actually receives the prescription in everyday practice, a mismatch geriatric specialists note makes it difficult to be fully confident the trial's safety findings apply equally to the older patients most commonly prescribed the drug today.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how confidently the trial's safety findings apply to typical patients receiving this medication?
options: Age has no bearing on how medications are metabolized or tolerated.
The findings are fully confirmed to apply equally to all patients regardless of age.
There is meaningful uncertainty about whether the findings fully apply to this older, more common patient group.
The trial population matched the typical patient population closely.
quests.correctAnswer: There is meaningful uncertainty about whether the findings fully apply to this older, more common patient group.
quests.hint: Think about what a mismatch between the trial's younger participants and the older patients actually receiving the drug suggests about the certainty of the safety findings for that older group.
quests.explanation: Geriatric specialists noting this age mismatch suggests genuine uncertainty about whether the trial's safety findings, established in a younger population, fully apply to the older patients who most commonly receive this medication in practice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Craft Fair Called 'Authentic' Selectively] The annual craft fair advertises itself as showcasing 'authentic, handmade regional goods,' a claim organizers apply to every vendor's booth uniformly, even though a fair employee acknowledges that roughly a quarter of vendors this year primarily resell imported items sourced from wholesale suppliers rather than making the goods themselves.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the accuracy of describing every booth at this fair as 'authentic, handmade'?
options: Every vendor at the fair makes their own goods by hand.
It accurately describes every single vendor at the fair.
It likely does not accurately describe a meaningful portion of the vendors present.
The organizers were unaware that any vendors resell imported items.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely does not accurately describe a meaningful portion of the vendors present.
quests.hint: Think about what an employee's acknowledgment, that a quarter of vendors resell imported goods, suggests about applying the 'authentic, handmade' label uniformly to everyone.
quests.explanation: An employee's acknowledgment that roughly a quarter of vendors resell imported goods suggests the fair's uniform 'authentic, handmade' claim does not accurately describe every booth present.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Retention Bonus Announced Ambiguously] The company announces a new retention bonus program 'for employees critical to our continued success,' a phrase left undefined in the initial memo, prompting widespread uncertainty among staff about whether the criteria refer to specific roles, performance rankings, or tenure, a question the company's HR department declines to clarify further when directly asked by several employees.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the company's communication regarding this bonus program?
options: It clearly and specifically defines exactly who qualifies for the bonus.
It was clarified in detail after HR was asked directly.
It leaves employees without clear information about who actually qualifies.
Every employee at the company automatically qualifies for the bonus.
quests.correctAnswer: It leaves employees without clear information about who actually qualifies.
quests.hint: Think about what leaving the qualifying phrase undefined, and declining to clarify when asked, suggests about how clearly this program has been communicated.
quests.explanation: An undefined qualifying phrase, combined with HR declining to clarify when directly asked, suggests employees have been left without clear information about who actually qualifies for this bonus.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Safety Record Measured Since a Reset Date] The factory proudly displays a sign reading '450 days since our last recordable incident,' a count that, according to a former safety officer, restarted after a change in how the company classifies incidents was quietly adopted, reclassifying several types of injuries previously counted as 'recordable' into a new, unreported category.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the meaning of this 450-day count?
options: It may reflect a change in classification as much as an actual improvement in workplace safety.
It certainly reflects only genuine improvement in workplace safety.
The reclassification made more incidents count as recordable, not fewer.
It has remained under the exact same classification system throughout.
quests.correctAnswer: It may reflect a change in classification as much as an actual improvement in workplace safety.
quests.hint: Think about what reclassifying certain injuries into an unreported category would do to a count that only tracks 'recordable' incidents.
quests.explanation: A classification change that moved certain injuries into an unreported category suggests the impressive day count may partly reflect this redefinition rather than solely a genuine improvement in actual safety outcomes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Data Center Powered by 'Renewable Energy'] The technology company claims its data centers run on '100 percent renewable energy,' a claim based on purchasing renewable energy credits equivalent to its total consumption, even though the actual electricity powering its servers, according to regional grid operators, is drawn from the same mixed-source grid, including fossil fuels, that supplies every other business in the area.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the actual electricity physically powering these data centers?
options: It is entirely generated from renewable sources with no fossil fuel involvement.
The renewable energy credits guarantee the physical electricity source.
It is physically separate from the grid supplying other regional businesses.
It likely includes energy from non-renewable sources, despite the company's stated claim.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely includes energy from non-renewable sources, despite the company's stated claim.
quests.hint: Think about the difference between purchasing credits equivalent to your usage and the actual physical source of the electricity reaching your building.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Best-Seller List Shaped by Bulk Orders] The book's appearance on a prominent best-seller list draws attention to its author, though publishing industry analysts note that a substantial portion of its reported sales came from bulk purchases made by organizations linked to the author's own speaking business, a detail the list's methodology does not distinguish from individual reader purchases.
quests.question: What can be inferred about what this best-seller ranking reflects?
options: It may reflect organized bulk purchasing as much as broad individual reader interest.
The list's methodology clearly distinguishes bulk orders from individual sales.
It reflects only broad interest from individual readers with no bulk purchases involved.
It excludes any purchases connected to the author's own organizations.
quests.correctAnswer: It may reflect organized bulk purchasing as much as broad individual reader interest.
quests.hint: Think about what a list methodology that doesn't distinguish bulk purchases from individual ones does to the meaning of a 'best-seller' ranking in this specific case.
quests.explanation: Since the list doesn't distinguish bulk purchases from individual ones, and a substantial portion came from organizations linked to the author, the ranking may reflect coordinated buying as much as genuine widespread individual reader interest.
